title: Ask HN: Is Agentic Coding really faster?
summary:
I am trying to get a grasp of what we can do with agents. I am an avid user of agentic coding. But somehow I think I code faster by hand (by IDEs I mean). I've always had a sketch approach to coding. Where I kinda lay out the pieces of what needs to be done and then finish them in chunks. That way you keep building a mental picture of what needs doing. Lately I've noticed something - its quite fast to analyze a new code-base with agents for sure especially messy ones. But once I do get a hold of the codebase (even larger ones), I can change things by hand quite quickly. My bottleneck seems to be typing, but manipulating the mental map is a lot faster.

Does this match other folks experience or am I deluding myself ?

title: Wix.com blocked account after I transfered .com domain
summary:
I paid for a .com domain transfer to wix.com using my bank card. After few weeks I logged to account and noticed that it's blocked. I opened a ticket and they emailed me requesting photos of my bank card and passport (never addressed the reason of block).

I asked why these documents were required and raised concerns about sending sensitive information by email. wix.com replied: "We cannot guarantee the security settings used by every email provider, so please do not send documents unless you are comfortable doing so."

However, they insist these documents are mandatory and refuse to make changes to my account or provide my domain authorization code until the review is complete.

So, I paid for the transfer, my account was blocked, and now I cannot access my domain or obtain its authorization code without sending sensitive documents through a channel wix.com itself admits it cannot guarantee is secure.

Has anyone experienced something similar with Wix? Is this normal practice, and what can I do to regain control of my domain?

title: Ask HN: A plea to help me help my father
summary:
My mother died in a car accident yesterday. To my great regret, I had constantly been putting off seeing her for years, and it leaves me deeply stricken that not only did she die with nobody at her side, but that she had spent years alone, with nobody keeping her company as she became isolated in older age.

While delivering the news, my father told me his doctor had given him two years to live, ten months ago. I don't want to repeat the same mistake. I want to spend the next year with him, fulfilling his dream of a cross-country road trip, something which he gave up on to raise me as a single father.

However, I cannot afford to do this. I did odd jobs here and there, but the kind of small-time contract work I dabbled in has dried up with the advent of LLMs, and my own savings are insufficient.

I would be incredibly grateful to be given a job opportunity with remote, flexible hours that would allow me to work while fulfilling my father's dream. I am not a conventional hire. I didn't finish high school, I don't have a formal employment history. I can offer a portfolio of personal projects but my resume is the kind that gets auto-rejected.

I can be incredibly useful, if you'll give someone the system overlooks a chance. I've spent 12+ hours a day for years programming all kinds of random things, most with no market value but which have developed my skills tremendously. I have experience with just about anything you can name, from embedded assembly and bare metal devops to Android apps and web dev and everything in between. On the off chance I don't, I'll learn anything you can throw at me. I simply love programming for programming's sake. I can wrangle a chatbot if that's what the job demands, but I prefer to use them for research and brainstorming and hand roll the best code I can myself, delivering something of far higher quality than you can get with prompting.

I have confidence in my own skills and that I can eventually break into the market on my own merits. But I don't have 'eventually'. My mother is dead and my father is dying. It's my own fault things ended up this way, not being the child I should have been for them earlier, and these regrets are mine to bear, but all I can do is ask for help to prevent another regret being added to the pile. I promise I will make it worth your while if you can give me a chance.

(A contact e-mail address is in the profile. Please forgive the anonymous account, it shames me to be begging like this... )

title: Ask HN: System One models for autonomous agents
summary:
I've seen a few impressive demos of Typesafe's new paradigm with System One models, and it seemed really clear to me that this was probably the direction the industry, especially for autonomous agents, was headed.

It's been a while though, and the major providers still seem to rely on more powerful LLMs (System Two) for all tasks, regardless of complexity.

Similar to how chain of thought arose, I thought the System One/System Two Thinking Fast and Slow model was one of those human structures that fit really well onto training neural nets, and I thought that this new paradigm could really change things.

That doesn't seem to be the case so far though, and I'm kind of puzzled to why this hasn't broken the industry open by now. Of course my predictions are not infallible, and one shouldn't expect much accuracy or for progress to abide by rigid schedules, but nonetheless: how come Kahneman Computer Use models aren't everywhere by now?

title: Ask HN: Why people keep posting AI-generated projects around the Internet?
summary:
Programming-related subreddits and other media platforms are current flooded by the waterfall of AI-generated projects. A typical post contains a problem description and the link to GitHub repo created just recently with sustainable amount of generated code in it. With the invite to review it, and to give a community feedback.

The quality of the projects vary, but very often these are codebases generated in a few days solely by the AI-agentic systems with little to no human review and prior history of development and recognition.

I'm asking this question not out of critiques. I genuinely don't understand motivation and the roots of this phenomena.

Asking for the professional code review seems to be pointless for the publisher. Many of them didn't have prior experience in the programming language in which the code has been generated. Furthermore, the code is seemingly not interested for the publisher either. It does not look to me as a good start for community-driven (F)OSS project anyway.

Another motivation that I can imaging is seeking for public recognition. But considering the amount of postings, I think it's highly unlikely in the current situation even for the genuinely high-effort works.

I can also assume that some are seeking for the self promotion by faking professional skills with AI assistance. That might be true for some, but the majority don't hide the fact that the presented code has been generated. It's unlikely the main motivation too.

So, I completely lost in understanding on what's going on, and what steams this never-stopping process. At a first glance the author doesn't gain anything in return, and I don't understand what they are seeking for.
